summary: PR #44254 perps order book — 49/49 recipe nodes passed against the live extension on Hyperliquid testnet, all captures via capture-helper. Three curated screenshots cover the visual ACs; AC3 (flag-off branch) and the compact half of AC5 are proven by test output instead, since neither renders in a reachable surface. 5/6 ACs PROVEN, AC5 UNTESTABLE for the compact popup layout.

standalone.label: AC1 — order book collapsed by default on the order entry page
standalone.note: ETH order entry page on arrival: the form fills the full width, no order-book panel and no resize divider are present, and the book toggle sits collapsed in the market header. Backed by two absence assertions (ac1-assert-book-collapsed, ac1-assert-divider-collapsed).

standalone.label: AC2/AC4/AC5 — expanded ladder with price levels, USD totals and the resizable split
standalone.note: AC2: one click on the header toggle expands the panel — 5 live ask rows, spread row, 5 live bid rows, cumulative depth bars and the Buy 51% / Sell 49% ratio. AC4: the same frame shows the 'Price / Total (USD)' headers with a USD cumulative total on every ask and bid row. AC5: form and panel share the width across the draggable divider. ⚠ For AC5 this proves ONLY the expanded/fullscreen layout — the compact (~360px popup) layout is NOT shown, because this CDP session exposes no popup target; that half rests on the order-book.utils width-clamp unit assertions and needs manual popup validation before merge.

standalone.label: AC6 — order form intact and limit price prefilled after tapping a bid row
standalone.note: After tapping a bid price row the order type switched to Limit and the Limit price field is prefilled with 1924.0; Size, Leverage, Auto close (TP/SL), Liquidation price, Margin, Fees and the submit button all still render beside the open order book. The Slippage summary row is absent by design (market-order only). reduce-only is not part of this new-order screen.

omit.reason: Pixel-near-identical to the AC2 capture (same screen, differing only in live tick values). AC4's claim — Price / Total (USD) headers with USD totals on both sides — is fully legible in the grouped AC2 image.
